notes: Activation and operations car: the console now answers the two questions a new owner actually asks - how do I activate this product, and how do I set up my bot - and closes every settings/E2E hole the human walkthrough found. New GET /api/setup renders an activation checklist: the three required slots with format rules mirrored from the aidog setup wizard (a parity test pins the mirror so it cannot drift), model-endpoint reachability probed live, and the chat-service state - each row carries a fix path that deep-links straight to the control that fixes it, and a fresh install sees a three-step welcome instead of a bare fail-closed status. The bot block shows token and allowlist presence (presence and format only, never a value) with a restart button: POST /api/service/restart kills and re-provisions the chat-service tmux session behind the Bearer gate, refuses honestly with 409 when no session exists, and never restarts the console itself. Writes that only take effect after a restart now say so - a restart hint appears after registry-at-start keys (tools_off/mcp/shell/context_dirs) and after setting the bot token or allowlist. The update banner gained real buttons: a manual check that busts the version cache and reports latest versus available as two honest states, and an Apply button that renders only when an update actually exists, runs the guarded updater detached and keeps polling through the console's own restart. The Overview system card can run the doctor on demand and renders its summary and lines verbatim. The cron job list can now delete a job (creation stays natural language in CHAT or /cron in Telegram, mirroring the CLI which never grew a form either). mycore.models and mycore.budget - previously read by the TG service and subagents but rejected by the console API with no control anywhere - are first-class validated keys with console inputs, so the per-task model whitelist and the compaction budget are configurable where people look. Two correctness bugs from the walkthrough are fixed: a console save used to rewrite settings from the validated view and destroy unknown hand-written keys - writes now merge onto the raw stored document - and the chat model client read only the process environment, so a MODEL_API_KEY written through the console never reached it - the key resolver now falls back env then secrets slot, env always winning. A hash watcher caught a latent hazard during the gate run: three older E2E harnesses rewrote the production secrets.env non-atomically (a truncation window was observed); all three now write atomically with temp plus rename at mode 0600, and E2E batches stay serial by rule. Suites after this car: core 1180/1180, console smoke 234/234, router 30/30, memory 58/58, setup 99/99, profile isolation 63/63, desktop shell 15/15, source lint 0 issues over 66 files, doctor 0F/0W, publish gate READY(0), console screenshot gate 7/7 js-clean, site gate ALL PASS (43 assertions); real-machine E2E: 18/18, 8/8, 44/44, 35/35, web3 read-only 33/33, web3 approval 61/61, frontend coverage 62/62, frontend UI 33/33, activation 81/81, activation UI 50/50. Locale packs: console 536 keys (en/zh parity), site pack 165 keys.
